Concept

A website concept for the board November 2026

From magazine to knowledge hub.

Eight issues of practical, independent writing on indoor air. This plan turns them into a website that answers readers' questions, finds the right expert, and knows who its readers are.

02 The AI website

Four helpers. One rule.

Each helper does the slow work so the editors can spend their time on judgement. None of them publishes anything on its own.

Writer helper

Turns a contributor's notes into a first draft in the house style, checks Australian spelling, and lists every claim that needs a source.

Expert finder

A reader types a problem, such as mould after a flood. The site shows the past articles on it and the named experts who wrote them.

Social posts

Every article gets draft posts for Facebook and LinkedIn, each linking back to the article, ready for an editor to change and schedule.

Reader Q&A

Readers ask questions in plain words. Answers come only from past issues, and every answer shows the issue and page it came from.

03 The reader CRM

Know who reads, writes and pays.

The live site's subscribe box looks like it works, but it saves nothing. I checked it in a browser: the form has no destination and the email field has no name, so a reader's address goes nowhere. The CRM fixes that first.

  • ReadersEveryone who subscribes, with the topics they open. Consent recorded, one click to leave.
  • ContributorsWriters and experts, their articles, their one business link, their next deadline.
  • SponsorsWho sponsors which issue, what was promised, and when it was delivered.
  • What's comingA shared calendar of issues, deadlines and events the whole board can see.
  • AI reader reportA plain-English note each month: what readers searched for and what they could not find.
  • Governance recordsBoard decisions, approvals and who signed off each change, kept in one place.

07 The authority plan

Become the source others cite.

Search engines and AI assistants send readers to sources they trust. Trust is built the slow way, and these five habits do it.

1Links from the field

Ask CASANZ, AIRAH and universities to link to the articles that help their members.

2Named experts

Every article carries a real author with a profile page and their qualifications.

3Sources on every article

Standards, studies and data are cited at the end of each piece.

4A steady schedule

Publish on a set rhythm the board can keep, not in bursts.

5Answer-ready writing

Each article opens with a short, direct answer, so AI search can quote it and credit IAQ Magazine.

Possible partners to approach:University of MelbourneNABERSWELL

08 Built to be found

Tell search engines what the magazine is.

Structured data is a small block of code that tells Google and AI assistants: this is a magazine, these are its issues, this is who publishes it. The live site has none. This page carries the full set.
